results.title: Redis Streams: an append-only log inside Redis
results.snippet: Streams are an append-only data structure with consumer groups, acknowledgements and pending lists.
results.content: Redis Streams store entries in memory with optional AOF persistence. Consumer groups give each message to one consumer; unacknowledged messages stay in a pending list and can be claimed with XAUTOCLAIM after an idle time. Retention is by length or ID, so a stream is usually short-lived work, not a long-term log.

results.title: Kafka: partitions, retention and replay
results.snippet: Kafka keeps a replicated, partitioned log on disk for days or forever, and consumers track offsets.
results.content: Kafka partitions a topic across brokers and replicates each partition. Consumers in a group split the partitions; ordering holds within a partition. Data is retained by time or size, so consumers can replay history. It scales to very high throughput, at the cost of running a cluster (and, historically, ZooKeeper or KRaft).

results.title: Choosing a queue for background jobs
results.snippet: For a work queue with a small team, Redis Streams are often enough; Kafka shines for event history and fan-out.
results.content: Rule of thumb: if you need a durable event history many services replay, use Kafka. If you need a work queue with acknowledgements and you already run Redis, Streams are simpler. Either way, keep the source of truth in your database and treat the queue as delivery.
